To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ion transport and water sorption/diffusion properties of polymer membranes can be predicted using the solution-diffusion model and Donnan theory, respectively, and that these properties are strongly dependent on the polymer and fixed charges.
the ion transport properties of charged polymers are governed by the ion-polymer interactions that control the partitioning of ions between the membrane and the surrounding solution.
the fixed charge groups in ion exchange membranes have significant effects on the membrane properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel polymer membranes with tailored properties for energy and environmental applications.
the synthesis, characterization, and modeling of ion-exchange membranes for use in energy conversion and environmental applications.
the synthesis of novel charged polymer membranes and their application in membrane-based processes, such as electrodialysis and polymer electrolyte fuel cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no universal membrane material that can be used for all applications.
the current understanding and modeling of ion transport in charged membranes is still in its infancy.
the current understanding of ion and water transport in charged polymers is still incomplete.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ion partitioning and ion diffusivity models are useful for describing ion transport in charged polymers and that the ion partition models are useful for predicting the salt permeability and conductivity in charged polymer membranes.
the ion transport properties of charged polymers are governed by the fixed charge groups, polymer structure, ion size and charge, and the ion-pair formation between fixed charges and counterions.
we are developing a better understanding of how to design and fabricate membranes for various applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ion partitioning model is a powerful tool for understanding ion transport phenomena in charged polymers.

the fundamental properties of ion exchange membranes can be understood in terms of the structure of the polymer and the fixed charge groups, and that this understanding can be used to design and develop new ion exchange membranes for various applications.
a fundamental understanding of the structure-property relationships of ion-containing polymers is necessary for the development of high-performance membranes for various applications.
